title: Concurrency kernel check-in (midweek journal)
content:
Midweek check-in notes from the kernel concurrency lab and KV/batching side-effects. This is a rough journal for the week — capture experiments, unexpected regressions, small hypotheses to try, and next steps. Treat as working notes; some items are incomplete and include 'notes to self'.

Attendees: Asha (owner), Miguel, Liang, Priya, Jordan (ops pairing for night window)
Meeting length: 40m standup + 30m adhoc pairing

High-level objective:
- Reduce p95/p99 tail caused by kernel lock contention during high-mix microbatching while preserving throughput.
- Ensure KV cache coherence doesn't regress prefix hit rate under the new concurrency schedule.

Quick snapshot metrics (prod-shadow):
- Baseline (Mon morning): p99 token latency 240ms, p95 85ms, throughput 3200 tokens/s per node, KV hit 72%
- After concurrency patch (canary): p99 310ms (regression), p95 92ms, throughput +6% (expected), KV hit 67% (unexpected drop)
- Observed correlation: spike in p99 corresponds to bursts where coalescer undoes prefill and causes re-warm cycles.

What we tried this week (experiments in lab):
1) Lock striping for kernel scheduling queue (PR-4812) — reduces coarse lock hold but increases queue hops. Observed +6% throughput, but p99 increased: hypothesis is increased reordering leads to KV shadow thrash.
2) Opt-in batch affinity window (config flag: affinity_ms=16) — keeps requests from same cohort on same kernel slice for short windows to preserve KV locality. Reduced KV miss rate back to 70% in lab, p99 improved slightly. Needs stress on mixed workloads.
3) Backpressure throttle tweak (soft-limit bump from 1.2->1.4×) — smoother throughput, reduced queue oscillations during traffic spikes but increased average latency by ~4ms (acceptable).

Signals & anomalies we flagged:
- Intermittent hotspot on kernel-3 (NY zone) that shows CPU steal-like patterns during async disk copy (eviction compact). Correlates with compact-trigger thresholds firing unexpectedly for some long-running sessions. Action: add richer trace to eviction path. (Liang)
- KV cache downstream instrumentation showed TTL expirations happening earlier than expected for some shadow entries — looks like background ref-count cleaning triggered by new lock order. Need to confirm if lock reordering changed lifetime assumptions. (Priya)
- Observed an edge where batching coalescer prefers lower-latency cohort but creates many small batches; this increases tokens/s but reduces amortized kernel work efficiency and favors throughput over latency. Consider dynamic latency-aware bucketing.

Decisions made in meeting:
- Revert coarse-grained lock in canary; keep lock-striping changes behind experiment flag until we validate affinity window across mixed traffic. (owner: Asha)
- Turn on affinity_ms=16 for canary traffic and run 48h mixed-workload soak. If KV hit >=71% and p99 < 260ms, roll forward. (owner: Miguel)
- Add eviction-trace logs only for the compact path and route to sampling storage (not full event log) to avoid IO blowup. (owner: Liang)

Action items (owner — due):
- Asha: prepare revert patch + branch release note and coordinate canary cut; target: 2029-06-20
- Miguel: deploy affinity window on canary pool and add dashboard panel for cohort-locality metrics; target: 2029-06-21
- Priya: instrument KV TTL/refcount path and run unit+integration tests under lock-stripe reorder; target: 2029-06-22
- Jordan: set up a 2-step smoke with simulated compact-trigger to reproduce NY hotspot; target: 2029-06-21 (night window)
- Liang: add compact-path debug traces (sampling) and a small perf test that triggers compaction deterministically; target: 2029-06-23

Open questions / hypotheses to validate:
- Does lock-striping increase cross-cohort scheduling so much that KV locality collapses? (need per-cohort scheduling heatmaps)
- Are eviction compactions being retriggered because of higher queue jitter (microbursting) rather than memory pressure? We suspect oscillation between coalescer and evictor.
- Is there an opportunity to do best-effort KV warming on kernel slice handoff to avoid cold-start misses? (tradeoff CPU for latency)

Short-term experiments to schedule:
- Controlled replay: 1h replay of mixed real-traffic (sample) with lock-striping + affinity_ms sweep [8,16,32] and export cohort-level KV hit heatmaps. (owner: Miguel)
- Prefill handshake: implement a tiny best-effort pre-warm on kernel handoff that does a non-blocking lookup of top-3 prefixes and populate local shadow at low priority. Aim to test on small canary only. (owner: Asha/Priya)

Notes to self / loose ideas (informal):
- Could try a small TTL extension for newly-warmed shadow entries when affinity window is high — preserve warm-up for the short term. But be careful with memory pressure.
- If coalescer is prioritizing throughput, maybe we add latency-sensitivity hints from caller metadata (edge-case for prioritized traffic). Work with product to see if we have route-level latency tags.

Risks / rollback criteria:
- If p99 > 300ms sustained for 30m on canary after any change -> immediate rollback of that change.
- If KV hit drops >5 percentage points and we cannot recover within 4h of tuning -> rollback affinity changes and block lock-striping rollout.

Next sync plan:
- Short sync Friday 30m: confirm canary metrics and decide whether to extend soak or roll forward.
- If replicate of NY hotspot happens, plan emergency triage (night-run) and bring SRE oncall.

Linked follow-ups (tickets & PRs):
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4812 (lock-striping prototype)
- JIRA: JIRA-ENG-4872 (kernel concurrency experiment tracker)
- Confluence: Kernel Concurrency Experiment page (internal design + perf charts)

End of notes.

-- Asha (midweek journal)

[quick checklist before Friday]
- verify dashboard panels show cohort-local hit rate + scheduling dispersion
- ensure sampling logs for eviction traces are <1% of events
- confirm night-run schedule with Jordan for deterministic compaction test

(rough scribbles / brainstorming included above; will convert to polished retro after Friday's decision)
summary: Working midweek journal covering kernel concurrency experiment, KV cache locality regression, affinity window trial, metrics snapshot, action items and next steps. Contains informal notes and short-term experiment plan.
